citation: Elias Colbert and Everett Chamberlin, Chicago and the Great Conflagration. Cincinnati and New York: C. F. Vent; Chicago: J. S. Goodman & Co., 1871.
author: Elias Colbert; Everett Chamberlin
describes_date: 1868 enumeration; city in 1871; fire of 8-9 October 1871
repository: Harold B. Lee Library, Brigham Young University, digitized by the Internet Archive
locator: pp. 146-147 ("An enumeration made in the spring of 1868 gave a total of 35,654 wooden buildings, and 3712 of brick and stone; total, 39,366"); p. 167, ch. XXXII "Chicago in 1871" (59,500 buildings: North 13,800, South 16,300, West 29,400); p. 226 (the ground north of De Koven Street "thickly studded with one-story frame dwellings, cow-stables, pig-sties, corn-cribs, sheds"); pp. 285-286 (West Division buildings burned "nearly all frame structures"; the South Division burned district held "the great majority of the most expensive structures in the city").
rights_note: Published in the United States in 1871; public domain by age. Only the counts and descriptions are used, no page images.
access_notes: Full text read on 2026-11-19 from the Internet Archive's OCR of the 1871 printing (identifier chicagogreatconf1871colb); the quoted passages were checked against the page numbers printed in that text.
what_it_supplies: A citywide ratio of building materials before the fire: in spring 1868, 35,654 wooden buildings to 3,712 of brick and stone (about nine in ten wooden).
The city's 59,500 buildings in 1871 by division, with the West Division largest (29,400).
Descriptions that the West Side's burned blocks were nearly all frame, and that the South Division's burned centre held the city's most expensive structures.
what_it_does_not_supply: A material for any particular lot, block or street; a material ratio by division or for 1871 itself; paint colours.
note: T-3683 uses the 1868 ratio and the division descriptions to set the share of frame and masonry stand-ins by district in the 1871 context city. The generated buildings remain anonymous reconstructions.
